title: always on top doesnt work when i open tabs in fullscreen

status.label: Needs focused investigation
status.detail: An Always on Top pinned window reportedly falls behind a full-screen video or tab and reappears when full-screen exits.

next_action.label: Reproduce and review proposal
next_action.reason: Always on Top uses the Windows topmost window band; a full-screen application may itself be topmost, so the pin sound alone does not establish a PowerToys defect.

judgment.rationale: Always on Top uses the Windows topmost window band; a full-screen application may itself be topmost, so the pin sound alone does not establish a PowerToys defect.
evidence: The reporter hears the pin sound on Windows 10.
The browser or application and full-screen mode are not specified.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the reported behavior and review the scoped proposal before implementation.

fix_assessment.rationale: Always on Top uses the Windows topmost window band; a full-screen application may itself be topmost, so the pin sound alone does not establish a PowerToys defect.

proposed_fixes.title: Investigate pinned-window ordering against full-screen applications
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: the full-screen window enters or changes topmost z-order after the pinned window; the application and behavior need confirmation before changing policy.
plan: Identify both windows and full-screen mode and reproduce while inspecting their topmost state.
Determine whether the behavior follows Windows topmost ordering or a PowerToys regression.
Only if a PowerToys-controlled defect is demonstrated, correct it with regression checks for normal full-screen and unpin behavior.
verification: Document the actual full-screen ordering and ensure normal pin and unpin still work without focus stealing.

information_gaps.information: The pinned window, full-screen application and how full-screen was entered
information_gaps.why_needed: Different full-screen modes can create a topmost window and alter z-order.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Name both apps and describe the full-screen action.

reproduce.title: Investigate pinned-window ordering against full-screen applications
setup: Pin a separate normal window using Always on Top.
steps: Enter the reported video's or browser's full-screen mode.
Observe ordering and compare with a non-full-screen window.
Exit full-screen and verify the pin state.
reproduce.expected_result: Pinned-window behavior is understood for the specified full-screen mode without disrupting normal pinning.

comment.body: Thanks for describing the pin sound and the window returning after full-screen exits. Full-screen modes can use different window ordering, so could you identify the pinned application, the application playing the video or showing the tab, and how you enter full-screen?
